title: This Car Is Designed to Crush.
narration: Inside, hidden structures fold and slow the car down over a longer distance and time.
Watch the front rails buckle and fold as the car slows all the way to a stop.
The rigid front stops in a tiny distance. The car bounces back almost immediately.
The passenger compartment keeps its shape. While the front folds inward, the cabin stays intact.
The front is meant to deform. The cabin isn't.

assumptions: Illustrative one-dimensional crash simulation: 50 km/h, 1400 kg, rigid barrier; crush stroke 0.62 m (crumple) versus 0.05 m (rigid counterfactual).
Not calibrated to any real vehicle or crash test; the rigid counterfactual is not a measured crash. No real injury figures are claimed.
The spoken comparison describes visible deformation, stopping distance and rebound in the simulated crashes.

Scope fixed by the owner (2026-11-16): 3D distance/time bars, force arrows and an occupant model are optional and NOT part of EP.04. Scenes s02c/s03/s04/s05b were re-described with the implemented real deformation, sequential comparison and cell highlight; no check was weakened (same not_obscured, timing, sound-off criteria, cell <=1 mm, rigid stroke <=6 cm).
